newsitem.title: USA: Dunavant pegs 97/98 US cotton crop 17.9 mln bales.
newsitem.headline: Dunavant pegs 97/98 US cotton crop 17.9 mln bales.

text.p: Memphis-based Dunavant Enterprises has estimated the 1997/98 U.S. cotton crop to total 17.9 million (480-lb) bales, chief executive officer and chairman Billy Dunavant said.
"We are on the high side of what the trade thinks," Dunavant said in response to an inquiry from Reuters.
On July 11, the U.S. Department of Agriculture estimated this year's cotton crop at 18.00 million bales, down from 18.94 million bales in 1996/97 (Aug/July).
Dunavant is a leading U.S. cotton merchant which handles a major portion of annual U.S. cotton exports.

"The number that I am giving to you is the number that we have developed from the existing acreage that the USDA has announced," Dunavant said. "If they (USDA) make any big adjustments up or down in acreage, then that will throw our number way out of kilter," he said.
Earlier on Tuesday, the Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies estimated 1997/98 U.S. cotton production at 17.642 million bales, trade sources reported.
Sparks declined to comment on the estimate.
Several other cotton analysts have pegged the new crop at between 17.4 million and 17.6 million bales.
The USDA will release its next estimate of this year's crop on August 12.
